messages:
maya: quick question about the async job API and client-side timeouts — how should we surface cancellation if the client disconnects or the client deadline elapses? thinking about backcompat and existing consumers who expect jobs to finish even if polling stops.

jon: short answer: we need an explicit, optional contract. currently we do 202 + status_url + poll token. we should NOT change default behavior (keep running) for BC. but add an opt-in field to request to signal "please cancel if client deadline passes".

maya: agreed on BC. proposal sketch: allow `client_deadline_ms` in the request body and `cancel_on_deadline: true` opt-in flag. server returns job_id as usual. if cancel_on_deadline is true, server should attempt graceful abort when wall-clock passes client_deadline. sample: 
```
POST /v1/async/process
Headers: X-Request-ID: 123e4567-...
Body: {"task": {...}, "client_deadline_ms": 120000, "cancel_on_deadline": true}
Response 202 Accepted
{
  "job_id": "job_abcd1234",
  "status_url": "/v1/async/status/job_abcd1234",
  "poll_token": "ptok_..."
}
```

rachel: couple of edgecases: 1) race where job finishes exactly when the server tries to cancel — we need deterministic terminal state. recommend server write a single terminal record (succeeded|failed|cancelled) with finished_at and optional result or error. clients can rely on idempotent reads from status_url. 2) cancellation should produce a stable error shape so SDKs can map to CancelledError.

sam: also add `Retry-After` and `next_poll_ms` hints in the status response so clients backoff correctly. e.g. status response while running: 
```
200 OK
{
  "job_id": "job_abcd1234",
  "status": "running",
  "progress": 0.47,
  "next_poll_ms": 500,
  "estimated_complete_ms": 30000
}
```
and server may set `Retry-After` for global rate guidance.

jon: regarding request IDs and idempotency — require X-Request-ID on submit; duplicate submit with same X-Request-ID should return the existing job_id and 409-like semantics avoided. also define semantics for reusing job_id vs creating new jobs.

maya: good call. For rollback/rollout: plan to add `cancel_on_deadline` as optional param (false by default). do a canary where new param is ignored by older infra so BC preserved. update SDKs to expose CancelledError and provide helper that sets client_deadline from its HTTP client timeout.

rachel: testing checklist: unit tests for race between cancel and finish, integration test that verifies terminal state written once, e2e with low timeouts (100ms) to ensure cancellation path is exercised, SDK behavior test for mapping error shapes.

sam: ops note: when customers turn on cancel_on_deadline we should expose a metric `jobs.cancel_requested` and `jobs.cancelled_successful` and `jobs.cancel_failed` so we can monitor cancellation reliability. also add a feature-flag to the control plane to toggle default behavior per-tenant.

maya: small UX detail — status_url should always eventually return a terminal body with `result` or `error` (even if cancelled) so clients don't have to guess. error shape recommendation: { "code": "cancelled", "message": "cancelled by client deadline" }.

jon: :thumbsup: one more thought — for long-running tasks where we can checkpoint partial outputs, include `partial_result_url` so the client can fetch what is available if they timed out but still want whatever was produced. optional field.

sre-bot: deploybot: canary rollout scheduled for next deploy window. tagging eng-platform-canary.

maya: plan: I'll draft a small RFC and add open PR with API contract + status schema + tests. assigning to @jon and @rachel for review. thanks all. :raised_hands:
